1. (Currently amended) A catheter system for delivering ultrasonic energy to a treatment site within a body lumen, the catheter comprising: a tubular body having a proximal end, a distal end and an energy delivery section positioned between the proximal end and the distal end; a plurality of ultrasound radiating members positioned within the energy delivery section, the plurality of ultrasound radiating members being allocated into at least three electrical groups comprising more than one ultrasound radiating member each; wherein the ultrasound radiating members of one electrical group are spatially interdigitated with the ultrasound radiating members of at least two other electrical groups in a non-uniform spatial distribution pattern.

2. (Currently amended) The catheter system of Claim 1, wherein the plurality of ultrasound radiating members are mounted on an inner core, wherein the inner core is configured for insertion into the tubular body, and wherein the inner core comprises a flexible support structure configured to maintain the spatial interdigitation of the ultrasound radiating members during insertion and deployment.

3. (Currently amended) The catheter system of Claim 1, further comprising at least one therapeutic compound delivery lumen that extends through the tubular body and terminates at least one outlet positioned in the energy delivery section, wherein the outlet is positioned in proximity to at least one ultrasound radiating member.

4. (Currently amended) The catheter system of Claim 1, wherein the ultrasound radiating members are interdigitated in a regular pattern with __a spacing of less than 0.5 millimeters between adjacent radiating members of different electrical groups__.

5. (Currently amended) The catheter system of Claim 1, wherein the ultrasound radiating members are interdigitated in a pseudo random pattern with __variable spacing between adjacent radiating members of different electrical groups__.

6. (Currently amended) A system for treating a patient having pulmonary embolism, the system comprising: a first and a second ultrasound catheters, each of the first and the second ultrasound catheter comprising a tubular body having a proximal portion and a distal portion, the distal portion comprising an ultrasound energy delivery section having at least one ultrasound element, the tubular body also including at least one fluid delivery lumen; and a control system connected to and configured to operate both the first and the second ultrasound catheters by independently controlling the ultrasound radiating members on each of the first and the second ultrasound catheters.

7. (Currently amended) The system of Claim 6, wherein the control system operates both the first and the second ultrasound catheters simultaneously with __phase-shifted ultrasonic signals to create a controlled acoustic field at the treatment site__.

8. (Currently amended) The system of Claim 7, wherein the control system is configured to independently control the ultrasound radiating members on the first and the second ultrasound catheters __to modulate the intensity and frequency of ultrasonic energy delivered to the treatment site__.

9. (Currently amended) A method for treating a patient having pulmonary embolism, the method comprising: advancing an ultrasound catheter comprising a tubular body having a proximal portion and a distal portion, the distal portion comprising an ultrasound energy delivery section comprising at least one ultrasound element and at least one fluid delivery lumen; advancing the distal portion of the ultrasound catheter to a treatment site in the patient's pulmonary artery; inflating a balloon on the distal portion of the ultrasound catheter; delivering a thrombolytic drug to the treatment site through the at least one fluid delivery lumen; and emitting ultrasonic energy at a frequency of between 20 kHz and 2 MHz to thereby promote diffusion of the thrombolytic drug at the treatment site.

10. (Currently amended) The method of Claim 9, wherein delivering the thrombolytic drug and emitting ultrasonic energy are performed simultaneously __with the ultrasonic energy enhancing the penetration of the thrombolytic drug into the thrombus__.

11. (Currently amended) An ultrasound catheter for treating a patient having pulmonary embolism, the catheter comprising a tubular body having a proximal portion and a distal portion, the distal portion comprising an ultrasound energy delivery section comprising at least one ultrasound element and at least one fluid delivery lumen, the tubular body defining a guidewire lumen extending through the proximal portion and the ultrasound energy delivery section, __wherein the ultrasound energy delivery section comprises a plurality of spatially interdigitated ultrasound radiating members allocated into multiple electrical groups__.

12. (Currently amended) The ultrasound catheter of Claim 11, wherein the guidewire lumen extends through the at least one ultrasound element __without disrupting the spatial interdigitation of the ultrasound radiating members__.

13. (Original) The ultrasound catheter of Claim 11, further comprising at least one balloon positioned at the distal portion of the ultrasound catheter.
